title: Orbifold Poincaré duality for torsion lattices
question: Uniform lattices with torsion act properly cocompactly on X=G/K, so the quotient is an orbifold rather than a manifold. Most Poincaré-duality references assume torsion-free groups. What is the right version of duality for \Gamma when the stabilizers are finite, and how does one see the dimension d=\dim X appear in the Bredon cohomology groups H^*_{\mathcal F}(\Gamma;\mathbb Q)?
answer:
The correct object is the Bredon (or equivalently, orbifold) cohomology of the \Gamma-action with coefficients in the constant rational Mackey functor. Because every finite subgroup H\subset\Gamma fixes a totally geodesic copy of X and acts trivially on the fundamental class, the Bredon chain complex C_*^{\mathcal F}(X) is a d-dimensional duality complex in the sense of Lück. Thus cap product with the \Gamma-invariant class \[X]\in H_d^{\mathcal F}(\Gamma;\mathbb Q) yields isomorphisms

\qquad H^i_{\mathcal F}(\Gamma;\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{\ \cap [X]\ } H_{d-i}^{\mathcal F}(\Gamma;\mathbb Q).

These Bredon groups agree with the singular cohomology of the orbifold X/\Gamma, so this is precisely the rational Poincaré duality satisfied by X/\Gamma. When \Gamma is torsion-free the collection of finite subgroups consists only of the trivial group, and the statement collapses to the familiar duality for manifolds. Hence \Gamma enjoys a rational PD of formal dimension d even though the quotient is an orbifold.
